subject: citation() in rstan version 2.0.1 is still listing version 1.3

messages.author: de0f441cbf692e7b
messages.subject: citation() in rstan version 2.0.1 is still listing version 1.3
parts:
Hi,

Thank for all the work that is placed into Stan. Today, I upgraded to
rstan v.2.0.1 and caught a minor typo. I have included my session info
at the end of this email in case you need it.

When I load rstan, R tells me the correct version:
library('rstan')
....clip....
rstan (Version 2.0.1, packaged: 2013-10-25 13:14:25 UTC, GitRev: 1a89615fac00)
....clip....

But the citation is still the old version:
citation('rstan')
....clip....
Stan Development Team (2013). Stan: A C++ Library for Probability and
Sampling, Version 1.3. URL http://mc-stan.org/
....clip....

Also, should I be using the "issue tracker" for problems such as this?
It's not really a bug, but more of a typo in the documentation.

Richard Erickson

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] citation() in rstan version 2.0.1 is still listing version 1.3
parts:
Yes, you can use the issue tracker for any issue we
need to fix. This lets us track them and associate
code fixes with the issues they fix.

Problems installing are a bit different, at least
until they've been reduced to a reproducible bug
that needs to be fixed in our code --- usually it's
some system state that doesn't correspond to Stan,
but to some assumption R or the environment is making
that we have no control over. On the other hand,
if we can code around the environmental or R problem,
then it's an issue again.

Let's just say the line's a little fuzzy :-)

- Bob
